sn15.1:1.7: Resolve _anamatagga_ as _ana’mat’agga_, where _ana_ is a doubled negative: “no known beginning”. | The idea stems from the the Nāsadīya Sūkta, which twice mentions “in the beginning” (_agre_), where from thought (_manaso_) evolved desire, before concluding, ”This creation—from where it came to be, if it was produced or if not—he who is the overseer of this (world) in the furthest heaven, he surely knows. Or if he does not know …?” (Rig Veda 10.129.7, Jamison/Brereton).
sn15.1:1.9: PTS has “a stack of squares” for caturangala, while BB curiously enough omits it entirely. But surely the meaning is as I have here. “small stick, tig” is a recognized meaning of ghatika.
